chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamilyah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

«It is not objectionable for the traveler to complete the prayer during a journey of two days' travel.» This report is also consistent with the general public (Sunni scholars), but action is not taken upon it because the amount in which shortening (qasr) is obligatory is the measure we mentioned, whether the journey is two days, less, or more. It is permissible to assume that the report is applicable to one who travels a distance less than what necessitates shortening, in which case completion (tamam) becomes obligatory upon him. And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what has been narrated:

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs
key_terms.لِلْعَامَّةِ: The general public (referring to Sunni scholars)
key_terms.مَسِيرَةَ يَوْمَيْنِ: A journey of two days' travel

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on completing prayers versus shortening them for a traveler in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the apparent contradiction between this report and the general consensus by distinguishing between the fixed distance threshold for obligatory shortening (qasr) and the duration of travel. He suggests the hadith may apply to those whose journey is shorter than the required distance, in which case completing prayers (tamam) is obligatory, thereby harmonizing the text with the principle that qasr is mandated only when the specific distance criteria are met.
